name: Cat Supplies Checklist
description: A category-by-category cat supplies shopping list for new kitten and adult cat owners.

items.note: Match kitten, adult or senior formula and keep the cat's current food during the transition

items.text: Cat treats for bonding and rewards
Litter box sized for the cat
items.note: Low sides for kittens; one box per cat plus one extra

items.text: Cat litter of your chosen type
Lined waste bin near the box
Cat tree or perch for climbing
Wand or teaser toys for interactive play
Small balls or mice for solo play
Catnip or silvervine toys if your cat responds
Brush or comb suited to the coat length
Cat shampoo for occasional baths if needed
Soft liner or familiar blanket for the carrier
Calming spray or familiar-scent item for vet trips

faq.q: What supplies do I need before bringing a cat home?
faq.a: Have food, food and water bowls, a litter box with litter, a scratching post, a few toys, basic grooming tools and a carrier ready before the cat arrives.

faq.q: How many litter boxes does a cat need?
faq.a: A common guideline is one litter box per cat plus one extra, placed in quiet, accessible spots. For a single cat, start with at least one box and add another if the home is large or multi-level.

faq.q: Do kittens and adult cats need different supplies?
faq.a: The categories are the same, but kittens need kitten-formula food, a low-sided litter box and smaller toys. Switch to adult food and adjust gear as the kitten grows.

faq.q: Should I ask a vet about diet and parasite prevention?
faq.a: Yes. This list is general guidance. Confirm food, vaccinations and flea and worm prevention with a veterinarian for your specific cat.

faq.q: Can I print this cat supplies checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can carry it to the store and check off each category as you go.
